test: the welcome page names the hotel, has the two-line heading and says what the board is for
what_should_happen: When the app opens on the welcome page, a small line above the heading reads "Harbour View · housekeeping". The big heading reads "Sixty rooms." with "No clipboard upstairs." on its second line, and a short paragraph under it says how every room moves through the day and what the board knows.
exact_words: Every room moves from occupied to dirty, cleaned, inspected and ready, raced against the day's arrivals.
The board knows where each one is, who is on it, and how long before its guest it was ready.

test: with every guest still in the counts read 60 rooms, 0 ready and 0 dirty
what_should_happen: On a fresh start every guest is still in their room. Once the page has read the rooms, its three counts read 60 rooms, 0 ready and 0 dirty.

reason: That the ready number is drawn in green is a colour, which a pretend browser does not paint.

test: with one room checked out the dirty count reads 1 and the other counts are unchanged
what_should_happen: Room 213's guest has checked out before the page opens. The counts come from the real hotel, so dirty reads 1 while rooms still reads 60 and ready still reads 0.

test: the picture shows rooms 209 to 215 of floor 2, each with its number and its state
what_should_happen: Beside the heading there is a small picture of a corridor. It shows exactly the seven doors 209 to 215 from floor 2, each with its number and its state word, which on a fresh start is Occupied. No other room number is in it.

test: the picture follows the hotel: a checked-out 213 shows as Dirty
what_should_happen: Room 213's guest has checked out before the page opens. The picture is drawn from the real rooms, so door 213 shows Dirty while 215 is still Occupied.

reason: Each state word drawn in its state's colour is a colour; the type shown on each door is checked on the board, where its words are given.

test: the doors are only a picture: clicking one does nothing
what_should_happen: Clicking a door in the picture, 209 or 213, does nothing. The address stays on the welcome page, the person cards are still there and no panel opens.

test: under "Who are you today?" four cards show Grace, Pradeep, Sunita and Mr Menon with their roles and blurbs
what_should_happen: Under the heading "Who are you today?" and its one-line note there are four person cards. Each card shows the person's name, their role, their one-line blurb and "Continue as" with their name.
exact_words: Each person sees their own screens. Everything they do changes the same hotel.
Runs housekeeping. Sees every room, assigns the dirty ones and inspects what others cleaned.
Checks guests out at the desk. The room turns dirty the moment he does.
Cleans the rooms she is given. Starts the clock when she begins and stops it when she is done.
Judges the morning on one number: how long before the guest each room was ready.

test: clicking 'Continue as Grace' changes the address to /supervisor/board
what_should_happen: Clicking Grace's card takes you to her first screen. The address becomes /supervisor/board.

test: clicking 'Continue as Pradeep' changes the address to /desk/checkout
what_should_happen: Clicking Pradeep's card takes you to the front desk's screen. The address becomes /desk/checkout.

test: clicking 'Continue as Sunita' changes the address to /housekeeper
what_should_happen: Clicking Sunita's card takes you to the housekeeper's screen. The address becomes /housekeeper.

test: clicking 'Continue as Mr Menon' changes the address to /manager/rooms
what_should_happen: Clicking Mr Menon's card takes you to the general manager's screen. The address becomes /manager/rooms.

test: Tab moves through the four cards in order
what_should_happen: Pressing Tab on the welcome page reaches Grace's card. Each further Tab moves to the next card: Pradeep, then Sunita, then Mr Menon.

test: Enter on a focused card opens that person's screen
what_should_happen: Tab until Sunita's card has the focus and press Enter. Her screen opens at /housekeeper, just as a click would open it.

reason: Below 1100px the cards going two per row, and below 1024px the picture moving under the heading, are layout, which a pretend browser does not draw.
At phone width the cards stacking one per row and nothing scrolling sideways are layout, which a pretend browser does not draw.

test: on the welcome page the header has the logo with "Harbour View · 60 rooms" and no ← or person button
what_should_happen: On the welcome page the header shows the RoomReady logo with "Harbour View · 60 rooms" beside it. Nobody has been picked yet, so there is no back button and no person button.

test: the logo on a person's screen opens the welcome page
what_should_happen: On Grace's, Pradeep's, Sunita's and Mr Menon's screens, the RoomReady logo is a link home. Clicking it opens the welcome page.

test: the ← button (Back to the home page) on a person's screen opens the welcome page
what_should_happen: On every person's screen there is a ← button at the left of the header, named "Back to the home page". Clicking it opens the welcome page.

test: on Pradeep's screen the person button shows his avatar, his name and 'Front desk'
what_should_happen: On Pradeep's Check out screen the right of the header has a button for the person you are. It shows his round avatar with the letter P, his name and "Front desk".

reason: The avatar being a round badge in the person's own colour is a drawing and a colour.

test: the person button opens "View the hotel as" with the four people and their roles
what_should_happen: Clicking the person button on Grace's board opens a menu headed "View the hotel as". It lists the four people in order, Grace, Pradeep, Sunita and Mr Menon, each with their role.

reason: The tick beside the current person is a drawing that screen readers skip, so only a real browser shows it.

test: choosing Pradeep on Grace's board closes the menu, opens Check out and shows Pradeep in the header
what_should_happen: With the menu open on Grace's board, choose Pradeep. The menu closes, his Check out screen opens at /desk/checkout, and the header's person button now shows Pradeep instead of Grace.

test: Esc closes the menu and you stay on the same screen
what_should_happen: Open the person menu on Grace's board and press Esc. The menu closes and you are still on the board, as Grace.

test: a click outside the menu closes it and you stay on the same screen
what_should_happen: Open the person menu on Grace's board and click somewhere on the page outside it. The menu closes and you are still on the board, as Grace.

test: Grace's title row has the tabs 'The board' and 'Work', the current one marked, and each opens the other
what_should_happen: On Grace's board two tabs read "The board" and "Work", and The board is marked as the page you are on. Clicking Work opens Grace's Work screen and marks Work instead, and clicking The board goes back to /supervisor/board.

reason: The current tab being filled with Grace's colour is a colour; which tab is current is tested.

test: Pradeep's, Sunita's and Mr Menon's screens have no tabs
what_should_happen: Pradeep, Sunita and Mr Menon each have one screen, and one screen is not a choice. Their title rows show no tabs at all, not even one for their own screen.

test: with every guest still in the Work tab has no badge
what_should_happen: On a fresh start no room is dirty and none waits for inspection. Once the rooms are read, the Work tab reads just "Work", with no number beside it.

test: with two rooms dirty and one waiting for inspection the Work tab counts 3
what_should_happen: Rooms 101 and 102 are dirty, and 103 has been cleaned and waits for inspection. The Work tab carries a badge that reads 3.

test: the Work badge changes when one of its rooms moves on, without anything clicked here
what_should_happen: Three rooms are dirty and the Work tab reads 3. Somebody elsewhere gives room 101 to a housekeeper, and within twenty seconds the badge reads 2 without anything clicked on this screen.

test: /supervisor, /desk and /manager land on /supervisor/board, /desk/checkout and /manager/rooms
what_should_happen: Typing a short address opens that person's first screen. The address /supervisor lands on /supervisor/board, /desk on /desk/checkout and /manager on /manager/rooms.

test: an address the app does not know, such as /kitchen, lands on the welcome page
what_should_happen: Typing an address the app does not have, such as /kitchen, does not leave you on an empty page. You land on the welcome page instead.

reason: The app's own slim scroll bar, dragging it and clicking its track need a real page height and a real mouse; a pretend browser has no layout.
Whether a page fits in the window depends on real heights, which a pretend browser does not measure.

test: by keyboard: Tab to the person button and Enter opens the menu
what_should_happen: On Pradeep's screen, press Tab until the person button has the focus. Pressing Enter opens the "View the hotel as" menu.

test: by keyboard: Tab reaches each person in the menu and Enter picks one
what_should_happen: With the menu open from the keyboard, Tab reaches each of the four people in turn. With the focus on Sunita, Enter closes the menu and opens her screen, and the header shows Sunita.

test: by keyboard: Esc closes the menu and puts the focus back on the person button
what_should_happen: Open the menu from the keyboard and Tab into it. Esc closes the menu, the focus goes back to the person button, and you stay on Pradeep's screen.

reason: Below 1024px hiding the hotel line and the person's name and role is done by the styles, which a pretend browser does not apply.
The header wrapping, the menu scrolling inside itself and the tabs scrolling sideways at phone width are layout, which a pretend browser does not draw.

test: on a fresh hotel the six cards read Rooms 60, Ready 0, Dirty 0, Being cleaned 0, To inspect 0 and On time —, each with its note
what_should_happen: Grace's board opens under "Harbour View · this morning" and the title "The board". On a fresh hotel its six cards read Rooms 60, Ready 0, Dirty 0, Being cleaned 0, To inspect 0 and On time —, each with its short note under the number.
exact_words: once a room is ready for a known guest

reason: The Dirty card turning red when a room is dirty is a colour, which a pretend browser does not paint.

test: Being cleaned counts the assigned rooms and the ones being cleaned together
what_should_happen: Room 101 is assigned to a housekeeper, 102 is being cleaned and 103 is still dirty. The Being cleaned card counts the first two together and reads 2, while Dirty reads 1.

test: four corridors, Floor 1 to Floor 4, each hold their fifteen doors in number order
what_should_happen: Below the cards there are four corridors, one for each floor, headed "Floor 1" to "Floor 4". Each holds its own fifteen doors in number order, 101 to 115 on the first floor up to 401 to 415 on the fourth.

test: a corridor's head says how many of its rooms are ready and dirty, e.g. '0 ready · 2 dirty'
what_should_happen: Rooms 101 and 102 are dirty and 214 has been made ready. The head of the Floor 1 corridor reads "0 ready · 2 dirty", Floor 2 reads "1 ready · 0 dirty" and Floor 3 reads "0 ready · 0 dirty".

test: every door shows its number, its type as Std, Dlx or Suite, and its state word
what_should_happen: Rooms on floor 1 are put into each state, from occupied through to ready. Every door shows its room number, its short type (Std, Dlx or Suite) and its state word: Occupied, Dirty, Assigned, Cleaning, To inspect or Ready.

reason: The coloured state strip on each door is a colour; the state word beside it is tested.

test: a room somebody is on names the housekeeper and the minutes since that step began, e.g. 'Sunita · 12m'
what_should_happen: Sunita started cleaning room 214 twelve minutes ago. Its door says Cleaning and also reads "Sunita · 12m".

test: left alone, the minutes on a door grow by themselves
what_should_happen: Room 214's door reads "Sunita · 12m" and nobody touches the board. Two minutes later the same door reads "Sunita · 14m" without anything being clicked.

test: a change made while Grace was on another screen is already on the board when she comes back
what_should_happen: While Grace is on Work, room 101 is checked out and 102 is checked out and assigned. When she clicks back to The board, door 101 already reads Dirty, door 102 Assigned, and the Dirty and Being cleaned cards both read 1.

test: under the corridors a legend names the six states: Occupied, Dirty, Assigned, Cleaning, To inspect, Ready
what_should_happen: Under the corridors there is a legend of the room states. It names exactly six of them, in the order a room goes through them: Occupied, Dirty, Assigned, Cleaning, To inspect, Ready.

reason: Each state's colour dot in the legend is a colour, and the legend sitting under the corridors is layout.

test: before the rooms are read no cards and no doors are drawn, then both appear
what_should_happen: At the very moment the board opens, before the rooms have been read, no count card and no door is drawn, so no untrue number shows. As soon as the rooms are read, the cards and all sixty doors appear.

test: Tab moves door by door in room order, each read out like 'Room 214, Deluxe, Occupied'
what_should_happen: Using only the keyboard, Tab reaches door 101 and then moves door by door in room order, through 115 and on to 201, up to 415. Each door is read out with its number, type and state, such as "Room 214, Deluxe, Occupied".

reason: A corridor's doors wrapping onto more rows below 1180px is layout, which a pretend browser does not draw.
The cards sitting three, then two per row on narrower screens is layout, which a pretend browser does not draw.
